newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sees dramatic increase in faulty loans.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sees dramatic increase in faulty loans.

text.p: The number of bad loans has increased dramatically in Colombia over the past year and the problem serves as a grim reminder of the country's economic slowdown, according to Colombia's Banking Association.

"The alarm system has been triggered and it shows that the economy continues heading toward the precipice of recession," the association said in a report focusing on what it said was a 72.8 percent increase in loan defaults between March 1996 and March 1997.
Leasing companies were especially hard hit, according to the report, which said there had been a 217 percent increase in foreclosures by such companies in the March-to-March period.

Banks experienced an 85.7 percent increase in faulty loans during the same time period, the report said, adding that the problem underscored the need to slash domestic interest rates and cut some of the bureaucratic requirements for restructuring loans.

The central bank's policy-making board of directors cut key interest rates by one percentage point earlier this month in a bid to breathe new life into the economy. But bankers complained that the move fell far short of what was needed to refuel growth, which totaled just 2.08 percent last year against average growth of 4.5 percent between 1985 and 1995.
Last year's slowdown has been cited as a leading cause of the fact that urban unemployment jumped to a nine-year high of 12.7 percent in the first quarter.
